newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Bourses bullish again, Ldn bounces on budget.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Bourses bullish again, Ldn bounces on budget.

text.p: Leading European shares followed New York's soaring Dow higher on Tuesday with London hitting a new trading peak ahead of the British budget and Frankfurt breaking records in both electronic and bourse trading.
In currency trading the dollar was steady against the mark but beneath a three-week high of 1.5237 touched in overnight dealings.
"It has come off a bit on profit-taking. But I think it's more the case of a stronger mark than a weaker dollar," said Adam Chester, senior analyst at Yamaichi International.

Against the yen the dollar was above overnight troughs and retaining its foothold above 112.00 yen ahead of the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) fourth-quarter tankan survey of business sentiment due at 2350 GMT.
Analysts said the BOJ's Tankan survey would be crucial to gauge what the Japanese economy is doing and where interest rates will go.

"If we get a strong Tankan, the yen will do well on the back of that, and we could see dollar/yen retracing back to 111.00 yen. But if it comes in line with expectations then, I don't see it having a major impact," said Yamaichi's Chester.

But the real exitement in European markets was on the stock exchanges after Wall Street soared 76 points or 1.71 percent overnight to pierce the 6,500 barrier for the first time -- its 11th record in 12 sessions and the biggest one-day points gain since August.

Britain's blue chip FTSE 100 index opened sharply higher ahead of Tuesday's budget, setting an intra-day record high at at 4,094.4, up 28.3 points, before slipping slightly. The previous FTSE record was 4,073.2, set on October 21.
Traders said hopes for a "prudent" non-inflationary budget (announcement begins at 1530 GMT) coupled with New York's performance had been the motive force.

"We are bound to start getting a bit nervous after the initial reaction to Wall Street," said one dealer. "I expect us to drift back and stocks to turn mixed until we see what (Chancellor) Clarke has to say."

Traders said they expected to see the corporate sector's tax burden increase to offset any drop in personal taxes designed to woo the electorate ahead of a general election which must be held by May next year.
In Frankfurt, German shares opened pre-bourse electronic dealings sharply higher at new peak and went on to open floor trading well above the previous all-time high.
The DAX 30 index was up 20 points at 2819.5 shortly after the bourse opened -- surpassing its previous trading record of 2,799.19 set on Monday.
Dealers said the boost came not only from Wall Street but also from the firmer dollar, which makes German exports more attractive.
In Paris, French shares firmed at the opening, with a jump of 0.34 percent on the CAC-40 index before retreating slightly.
CURRENCIES AT 1000 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 112.45 yen and 1.5232 marks against 112.62 yen and 1.5208 marks late on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1000 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was 24.9 points higher at 4,079.5.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 2.08 points at 2,279.22.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was up 14.26 at 2,813.45.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold opened a touch weaker at $374.75 compared with Monday's close of $375.05. Silver was down five cents at $4.76.
